points.title: 把 — doing something to an object
points.explain: 把 moves the object before the verb to show what you do to it and how it ends up. The verb must have something after it, such as a result, direction or 了. Pitfall: you cannot end with a bare verb (not 我把书看).

examples.en: Please close the door.
I finished my homework.
He left his phone at home.

examples.text: 你把这本书放在桌子上吧。
examples.en: Put this book on the table.

points.title: 把 with negation and modal verbs
points.pattern: Subject + 没/不/要 + 把 + Object + Verb + …
points.explain: In a 把 sentence, negatives like 没 and 不 and modal verbs like 要, 能, 应该 go before 把, not before the verb. Pitfall: 我把门没关 is wrong; say 我没把门关上.

examples.en: I didn't bring the money.
Don't get your clothes dirty.
I'm going to clean the room.

examples.text: 他不想把这件事告诉别人。
examples.en: He doesn't want to tell others about this.

points.title: 把…当作/变成/翻译成 — turning A into B
points.pattern: Subject + 把 + A + Verb成/作 + B
points.short: 把 A into B (变成, 当作)
points.explain: 把 A + verb + 成/作 + B means treating, turning or translating A into B. Common verbs are 变成, 当作, 翻译成, 换成, 看成. Pitfall: 成 must follow the verb directly.

examples.en: Please write these as Chinese characters.
He treats me as a good friend.

examples.text: 我想把美元换成人民币。
examples.en: I want to change dollars into RMB.
Don't write 大 as 太.

points.title: 被 — the passive voice
points.explain: 被 marks the passive: the subject receives the action, and the doer can follow 被 or be left out. It often describes something unpleasant or unexpected. Pitfall: like 把, the verb usually needs a result or 了 after it.

examples.text: 我的自行车被人骑走了。
examples.en: Someone rode off on my bike.
The cake was eaten up by my little brother.
He was criticized by the teacher.
The cup was broken by me.

points.title: 叫/让 — spoken passive
points.pattern: Receiver + 叫/让 + Doer + Verb + Result
points.short: spoken passive with 叫 or 让
points.explain: In speech, 叫 and 让 can replace 被 to form a passive. Unlike 被, they must be followed by the doer. Pitfall: 我的书让偷了 is wrong; the doer cannot be left out.

examples.en: Someone took my umbrella.
The kid got the clothes dirty.

examples.text: 那块蛋糕叫猫吃了一半。
examples.en: The cat ate half of that cake.
He overheard what I said.

points.title: Potential complement: V得 + result
points.explain: Verb + 得 + result says the action is possible, for example 看得见 'can see'. It focuses on whether the result can be reached. Pitfall: don't confuse it with the degree complement 跑得快 'runs fast'.

examples.text: 黑板上的字你看得清楚吗？
examples.en: Can you see the words on the board clearly?
We can finish this much food.
He speaks Chinese and I can understand it.
Can you come back before eight?

points.title: Potential complement: V不 + result
points.explain: Verb + 不 + result says the action can't reach its result, for example 听不懂 'can't understand'. It is more natural than 不能 for physical or mental limits. Pitfall: 不能听懂 is unnatural; say 听不懂.

examples.text: 老师说得太快，我听不懂。
examples.en: The teacher speaks too fast; I can't understand.
The box is too heavy; I can't carry it.
I can't finish today's homework.
The door is shut; I can't get in.

points.title: V得了/V不了 — able or unable
points.explain: 得了 and 不了 (liǎo) after a verb say whether something can happen at all, or whether there is too much to finish. 吃不了 can mean 'can't eat it' or 'can't eat that much'. Pitfall: 了 here is read liǎo, not le.

examples.en: I can't go tomorrow.
I can't eat this much food.
Can you manage it by yourself?
He's sick and can't come.

points.title: Degree complement with 得
points.short: how an action is done: V得 + adj
points.explain: Verb + 得 + description says how well or how something is done: 她唱得很好. If there is an object, repeat the verb: 他说中文说得很流利. Pitfall: don't put the object between the verb and 得.

examples.en: She sings beautifully.
You came really early today.
He runs faster than me.
You handled this wrongly.

points.title: 极了/死了/坏了 — extremely
points.pattern: Adjective + 极了 / 死了 / 坏了
points.explain: Adjective + 极了 means 'extremely'. In speech, 死了 and 坏了 also mean 'terribly', often for feelings or bad states. Pitfall: don't add 很 before the adjective (not 很好极了).

examples.en: The weather today is excellent.
I'm starving, let's eat!

examples.text: 听到这个消息，他高兴坏了。
examples.en: He was overjoyed at the news.
This dish is delicious.

points.title: V得 + result clause — so … that
points.explain: 得 can introduce a whole clause that shows the result of a strong state, like 'so tired that I can't walk'. The clause describes what happened because of the degree. Pitfall: the part after 得 is a full description, not just one adjective.

examples.en: He laughed so hard he couldn't speak.
I'm so tired I don't want to move.
She was so anxious that she started crying.

examples.text: 孩子们高兴得跳了起来。
examples.en: The children jumped up with joy.

points.title: Compound directional complements
points.pattern: Verb + 上/下/进/出/回/过/起 + 来/去
points.short: compound direction: 走进来, 跑出去
points.explain: A verb can take a two-part direction: 上/下/进/出/回/过/起 plus 来 (toward the speaker) or 去 (away). A place word goes before 来/去: 走进教室来. Pitfall: don't put the place after 来/去.

examples.en: He came down from upstairs.
The teacher walked into the classroom.
The puppy ran out.
Please bring the book back.

points.title: V起来 — start to; when doing
points.explain: 起来 after a verb or adjective can mean an action or state starts, like 下起雨来 'it started to rain'. 看起来 / 听起来 mean 'it looks / sounds'. Pitfall: an object goes between 起 and 来.

examples.en: The weather is gradually getting hot.
This dish looks delicious.
Suddenly it started to rain.
Easier said than done.

points.title: V下去 — keep on doing
points.explain: 下去 after a verb means to keep doing something that has already started. It is common with 说, 学, 坚持 and 住. Pitfall: don't confuse it with the literal 'go down', like 走下去.

examples.en: Please go on.
You need to keep studying.
It can't go on like this.
I want to keep living here.

points.title: V出来 — figure out, come up with
points.explain: 出来 after a verb can mean something becomes known or produced: 看出来 'notice', 想出来 'come up with', 听出来 'recognize by sound'. Pitfall: 想出来 means coming up with an idea, while 想起来 means remembering.

examples.en: I recognized your voice.

examples.text: 你看出来他不高兴了吗？
examples.en: Did you notice he was unhappy?
I came up with a good idea.
I can't write this character.

points.title: V下来 — record, stop, settle
points.short: fix or settle down: V下来
points.explain: 下来 after a verb can mean something is kept or fixed, as in 记下来 'write down' and 留下来 'stay'. With adjectives, it means calming or slowing down: 安静下来. Pitfall: 下来 is about settling or staying, while 下去 is about continuing.

examples.en: Please write down his name.

examples.text: 教室里慢慢安静下来了。
examples.en: The classroom gradually quieted down.
The car slowly came to a stop.
He decided to stay and work.

points.title: 越来越 — more and more
points.explain: 越来越 + adjective means something is getting more and more so over time. Don't add 很 or 非常 after 越来越. Pitfall: 越来越很冷 is wrong; say 越来越冷.

examples.en: It's getting colder and colder.
His Chinese is getting better and better.
There are more and more cars in the city.
I like it here more and more.

points.title: 越…越… — the more…, the more…
points.short: the more A, the more B
points.explain: 越 A 越 B means 'the more A, the more B': B changes as A increases. Both parts need 越. Pitfall: don't add 很 after 越.

examples.en: The rain outside is getting heavier and heavier.
The more I read this book, the more I like it.
The more he talked, the happier he got.
The more anxious you are, the more mistakes you make.

points.title: 比 with 更/还/一点儿/多了
points.pattern: A + 比 + B + (更/还) + Adj + (一点儿/多了)
points.short: comparison details: 更, 一点儿
points.explain: In 比 comparisons, 更 or 还 before the adjective mean 'even more'. 一点儿 or 多了 after it show a small or big difference. Pitfall: never use 很 or 非常 in a 比 sentence.

examples.en: Today is even hotter than yesterday.
He's a little taller than me.

examples.text: 这个房间比那个大多了。
examples.en: This room is much bigger than that one.
The younger sister is even smarter than the older one.

points.title: 比 with exact difference
points.pattern: A + 比 + B + Adj + Number + Measure
points.explain: To say exactly how big the difference is, put the amount after the adjective: 他比我大两岁. The amount always follows the adjective. Pitfall: 他比我两岁大 is wrong.

examples.en: My brother is three years older than me.
This one is fifty yuan more expensive than that one.
He arrived ten minutes earlier than me.
I'm two kilos heavier than last year.

points.title: 没有…那么/这么 — not as … as
points.pattern: A + 没有 + B + 那么/这么 + Adj
points.explain: A 没有 B 那么 + adjective means 'A is not as … as B'. 那么 or 这么 adds emphasis. Pitfall: don't use 比 with 不 for this meaning; 不比 means something else.

examples.en: Beijing isn't as cold as the Northeast.
I'm not as tall as him.
Today isn't as hot as yesterday.
Riding isn't as tiring as walking.

points.title: A 不如 B — A is not as good as B
points.short: A not as good as B: 不如
points.explain: A 不如 B means 'A is not as good as B', or not as good in some way if an adjective follows. 不如 can also suggest a better choice: 不如明天去. Pitfall: the adjective after 不如 B is usually positive.

examples.en: My Chinese isn't as good as his.
Taking the bus is not as fast as cycling.

examples.text: 今天太晚了，不如明天去。
examples.en: It's too late today; we might as well go tomorrow.
This restaurant isn't as good as that one.

points.title: 好像 — seem, as if
points.explain: 好像 means 'it seems' or 'as if' and makes a statement softer or less certain. It can go before the subject or the verb. Pitfall: 好像…一样 is a comparison, while 好像 alone just shows uncertainty.

examples.en: He seems to be sick.
It seems to be raining outside.
I think I've seen you somewhere.

examples.text: 她高兴得好像孩子一样。
examples.en: She was as happy as a child.

points.title: 除了…以外，还/也 — besides
points.pattern: 除了 + A + (以外)，Subject + 还/也 + …
points.explain: 除了 A 以外，还/也 B means 'besides A, also B', so A is included. Use 还 or 也 in the second part. Pitfall: if the second part has 都, A is left out.

examples.text: 除了中文以外，我还学英语。
examples.en: Besides Chinese, I also study English.

examples.text: 除了米饭，他也喜欢面条。
examples.en: Besides rice, he also likes noodles.

examples.text: 除了周末以外，我晚上也有空。
examples.en: Besides weekends, I'm also free in the evenings.

examples.text: 除了打球，他还喜欢游泳。
examples.en: Besides playing ball, he also likes swimming.

points.title: 除了…以外，都 — except
points.explain: 除了 A 以外，都 … means 'everyone or everything except A'. With 都, A is left out of the group. Pitfall: don't use 还 here, or the meaning becomes 'besides'.

examples.en: Everyone came except Xiao Wang.

examples.text: 除了星期天以外，我每天都上班。
examples.en: I work every day except Sunday.
I eat everything except fish.

examples.text: 除了他以外，我们都同意。
examples.en: All of us agree except him.

points.title: 不但…而且… — not only…but also
points.pattern: Subject + 不但 + A，而且 + B
points.short: not only A but also B
points.explain: 不但 A，而且 B means 'not only A, but also B', where B adds more. Often 也 or 还 follows in the second part. Pitfall: if the subjects differ, put 不但 before the first subject.

examples.en: She's not only pretty but also smart.

examples.text: 这家店不但便宜，而且好吃。
examples.en: This place is not only cheap but tasty.
He can not only speak but also write.
Not only am I going, he is too.

points.title: 既…又… — both … and …
points.short: both A and B: 既…又
points.explain: 既 A 又 B means something is both A and B at the same time. A and B are usually adjectives or verbs of the same kind. Pitfall: both parts should be all positive or all negative.

examples.text: 这个房间既干净又安静。
examples.en: This room is both clean and quiet.
He's both a teacher and a friend.
Doing it this way saves money and is convenient.
She can both sing and dance.

points.title: 只要…就… — as long as
points.explain: 只要 A，就 B means 'as long as A, then B': A is enough for B to happen. 就 comes after the subject in the second part. Pitfall: don't mix it with 只有…才, which means A is required.

examples.en: As long as you work hard, you'll learn well.
As long as you come, I'm happy.
As long as it doesn't rain, we'll go.
Whenever he has time, he reads.

points.title: 只有…才… — only if
points.explain: 只有 A，才 B means 'only if A, then B': A is the one necessary condition. Always use 才, not 就, in the second part. Pitfall: 只有…就 is wrong.

examples.en: Only with lots of practice can you speak well.
Only he knows about this.
Only on weekends am I free.
Only by being serious can you do it well.

points.title: 如果…(的话)，就… — if … then
points.pattern: 如果 + Condition (+ 的话)，(Subject) + 就 + Result
points.explain: 如果 A (的话)，就 B means 'if A, then B'. 的话 at the end of the condition is optional and common in speech. Pitfall: 就 goes after the subject of the second part, never before it.

examples.text: 如果明天下雨，我们就不去了。
examples.en: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.

examples.text: 如果你累了的话，就休息吧。
examples.en: If you're tired, rest.
If you have questions, ask the teacher.
If I had money, I'd buy a house.

points.title: 要是…就… — if (spoken)
points.explain: 要是 means 'if' like 如果, but it sounds more casual and spoken. It often pairs with 就 or ends with 的话. Pitfall: don't confuse it with 要 'want', since 要是 is one word.

examples.text: 要是你不想去，就别去了。
examples.en: If you don't want to go, then don't.
If you're free, come over.

examples.text: 要是早知道，我就不来了。
examples.en: If I'd known, I wouldn't have come.
What if we're late?

points.title: 连…都/也… — even
points.explain: 连 X 都/也 means 'even X' and points out a surprising or extreme case. 都 or 也 must follow. Pitfall: forgetting 都 or 也 makes the sentence wrong.

examples.en: He left without even eating.

examples.text: 这个字连老师也不认识。
examples.en: Even the teacher doesn't know this character.
I was so busy I didn't even drink water.
Even little kids know that.

points.title: 一…就… — as soon as
points.pattern: Subject + 一 + Action A + 就 + Action B
points.explain: 一 A 就 B means 'as soon as A, B happens', or 'every time A, B'. Both 一 and 就 go before verbs. Pitfall: if there are two subjects, 一 comes after the first and 就 after the second.

examples.text: 我一到家就给你打电话。
examples.en: I'll call you as soon as I get home.
His face turns red whenever he drinks.
As soon as the teacher explained, I understood.
As soon as it got dark, the street lights came on.

points.title: 对…来说 — for someone
points.explain: 对 X 来说 means 'for X' or 'as far as X is concerned', and gives someone's point of view. It usually starts the sentence. Pitfall: don't confuse it with 对…说 'say to someone'.

examples.en: For me, Chinese characters are hard.
For kids, playing is important.
For him, this isn't a problem.

examples.text: 对学生来说，学习最重要。
examples.en: For students, studying matters most.

points.title: 是…的 — emphasizing details of a past event
points.pattern: Subject + 是 + Time/Place/Manner + Verb + 的
points.explain: 是…的 stresses when, where, how or with whom a past action happened. Put the detail after 是 and 的 at the end, or before the object. Pitfall: use it only for actions already done, and 是 can be left out in positive sentences.

examples.en: When did you come?
I came by plane.
This book was bought in Beijing.
I didn't go alone.

points.title: 难道…吗 — surely not?
points.explain: 难道…吗 makes a rhetorical question that shows surprise or disbelief. The speaker means the opposite of what is asked. Pitfall: it isn't a real question, so don't answer it with yes or no.

examples.en: Don't tell me you don't know?
Surely he isn't late again?

examples.text: 这么简单，难道你不会吗？
examples.en: It's so easy, surely you can do it?
Can this really be true?

points.title: 不是…吗 — isn't it…?
points.explain: 不是…吗 is a rhetorical question meaning 'isn't it …?' and reminds someone of a known fact. It often sounds a little surprised or blaming. Pitfall: the meaning is positive: 你不是去过吗 means 'you have been there'.

examples.en: Didn't you say you'd come today?
Isn't he your older brother?
Isn't this simple?
Haven't you been to Shanghai?

points.title: 怎么/哪儿 rhetorical questions
points.explain: Question words like 怎么, 哪儿 and 谁 can make rhetorical questions that mean a strong 'no'. 我哪儿知道 means 'how would I know'. Pitfall: these are not real questions; they express denial.

examples.en: How could I forget you?

examples.text: 我哪儿知道他去哪儿了？
examples.en: How would I know where he went?
Who doesn't want to travel?
It's so expensive, how could I afford it?

points.title: 既然…就… — since … then
points.pattern: 既然 + Known fact，(Subject) + 就 + Conclusion
points.explain: 既然 A，就 B means 'since A is true, then B'. A is a fact both people already know, and B is a suggestion or conclusion. Pitfall: unlike 因为, 既然 is not used for new information.

examples.text: 既然你病了，就在家休息吧。
examples.en: Since you're sick, rest at home.
Since you're here, stay a few more days.

examples.text: 既然你不喜欢，就别买了。
examples.en: Since you don't like it, don't buy it.

examples.text: 既然决定了，就别再想了。
examples.en: Since you've decided, stop thinking about it.

points.title: 不管…都… — no matter
points.explain: 不管 A，都 B means 'no matter A, B still happens'. A must have a question word or two choices, like 多忙 or 去不去. Pitfall: 不管很忙 is wrong; say 不管多忙.

examples.en: No matter how busy, he goes running.
Whether you go or not, I'm going.
Whoever comes, I welcome them.

examples.text: 不管天气怎么样，我们都出发。
examples.en: Whatever the weather, we'll set off.

points.title: 由于 — due to, because of
points.pattern: 由于 + Cause，(所以/因此) + Result
points.explain: 由于 means 'due to' or 'because of' and is more formal than 因为. It often pairs with 所以 or 因此. Pitfall: 由于 usually starts the sentence, while 因为 can also come second.

examples.en: Due to snow, the plane was late.
Because of poor health, he didn't come.

examples.text: 由于时间关系，我们先走了。
examples.en: Due to time, we're leaving first.
Thanks to hard work, he did well on the exam.

points.title: 因此 — therefore
points.explain: 因此 means 'therefore' or 'for this reason' and links a cause to a result. It is a bit more formal than 所以. Pitfall: 因此 starts the result clause and is not used before the cause.

examples.en: He was sick, so he didn't go to work.

examples.text: 路上车太多，因此我迟到了。
examples.en: There was traffic, so I was late.

examples.text: 她很努力，因此进步很快。
examples.en: She works hard, so she improves fast.

examples.text: 天气不好，因此比赛取消了。
examples.en: The weather was bad, so the match was canceled.

points.title: 于是 — so, thereupon
points.explain: 于是 means 'so' or 'then' and shows that event B happened because of A. It is used in stories about the past. Pitfall: 于是 isn't used for advice or future plans; use 所以 there.

examples.text: 天黑了，于是我们回家了。
examples.en: It got dark, so we went home.

examples.text: 他很饿，于是去买了面包。
examples.en: He was hungry, so he went to buy bread.

examples.text: 我没听懂，于是又问了一遍。
examples.en: I didn't understand, so I asked again.
It rained, so the game stopped.

points.title: 先…再/然后… — first … then
points.explain: 先 A 再 B means 'first A, then B'. 然后 can also link the steps, and 最后 marks the last step. Pitfall: 再 is used for actions not yet done; for the past, use 然后 or 又.

examples.en: Let's eat first, then see a movie.
Wash your hands first, then eat.
Rest first, then do your homework.

examples.text: 他先去银行，然后去了超市。
examples.en: He went to the bank first, then the supermarket.

points.title: 不是…而是… — not A but B
points.short: not A but B: 不是…而是
points.explain: 不是 A，而是 B means 'not A, but B' and corrects a wrong idea. A and B should be the same kind of thing. Pitfall: don't confuse it with 不是 A 就是 B 'either A or B'.

examples.en: He's not a teacher but a student.

examples.text: 我不是不想去，而是没时间。
examples.en: It's not that I don't want to go, I don't have time.
The problem isn't money but time.
This isn't mine, it's his.

points.title: 不是…就是… — either … or
points.short: either A or B: 不是…就是
points.explain: 不是 A 就是 B means 'if not A, then B', so it is always one of the two. It often describes habits or guesses. Pitfall: it doesn't mean 'not A but B'.

examples.text: 他周末不是看书就是睡觉。
examples.en: On weekends he either reads or sleeps.

examples.text: 这几天不是刮风就是下雨。
examples.en: These days it's either windy or rainy.

examples.text: 她不是在学校就是在家。
examples.en: She's either at school or at home.

examples.text: 门口那个人不是小王就是小李。
examples.en: That person at the door is either Xiao Wang or Xiao Li.

points.title: 为了 — in order to
points.explain: 为了 means 'in order to' or 'for' and comes before the goal at the start of the sentence. The action comes after. Pitfall: don't use 因为 for purpose; 因为 is for causes.

examples.text: 为了身体健康，他每天跑步。
examples.en: He runs every day to stay healthy.

examples.text: 为了学好中文，她去了中国。
examples.en: She went to China to learn Chinese well.

examples.text: 为了孩子，妈妈很努力工作。
examples.en: Mom works hard for her kids.
I got up early so as not to be late.

points.title: 关于 — about, concerning
points.pattern: 关于 + Topic，… / 关于 + Topic + 的 + Noun
points.explain: 关于 means 'about' or 'concerning' and introduces a topic. It can start a sentence or describe a noun with 的. Pitfall: 关于 can't come after the subject; use 对 for that.

examples.text: 这是一本关于历史的书。
examples.en: This is a book about history.

examples.text: 关于这件事，我不太清楚。
examples.en: I'm not too clear about this matter.

examples.text: 我们说了关于工作的事。
examples.en: We talked about work.
Do you have questions about the exam?

points.title: 对 / 对于 — toward, regarding
points.explain: 对 introduces the person or thing an attitude or action is directed at: 他对我很好. 对于 is more formal and usually starts the sentence. Pitfall: 对 can come after the subject, but 对于 is rarely used there.

examples.en: The teacher is very kind to us.

examples.text: 我对中国文化很感兴趣。
examples.en: I'm very interested in Chinese culture.

examples.text: 对于这个问题，大家意见不同。
examples.en: People have different views on this question.
Drinking is bad for your health.

points.title: 根据/按照 — according to
points.explain: 根据 means 'according to' or 'based on', usually information. 按照 means 'following' a rule or plan. Both start a phrase before the main verb. Pitfall: use 按照 for instructions and 根据 for evidence.

examples.text: 根据天气预报，明天有雨。
examples.en: According to the forecast, it'll rain tomorrow.
Please do the homework as required.
We set off according to plan.
According to the survey, everyone likes it.

points.title: 通过 — through, by means of
points.explain: 通过 means 'through' or 'by means of' and shows how something is achieved. It can also be a verb meaning 'to pass', like 通过考试. Pitfall: put the means right after 通过, before the result.

examples.en: I met him through a friend.
Through hard work, he succeeded.
I passed this exam.

examples.text: 通过上网，我们可以学很多。
examples.en: We can learn a lot online.

points.title: 随着 — along with, as
points.explain: 随着 means 'along with' or 'as' and shows that one change brings another. It usually starts the sentence and is followed by a noun phrase of change. Pitfall: the result often uses 越来越 or 了.

examples.text: 随着年纪变大，他更懂事了。
examples.en: As he got older, he became more sensible.

examples.text: 随着天气变冷，人们穿得多了。
examples.en: As it gets colder, people wear more.

examples.text: 随着时间过去，我忘了他。
examples.en: As time passed, I forgot him.

examples.text: 随着发展，城市越来越大。
examples.en: With development, the city keeps growing.

points.title: 向/往 — toward a direction
points.explain: 向 and 往 mean 'toward' and show direction before a verb: 往前走 'walk forward'. 向 can also mean 'to a person', as in 向老师学习. Pitfall: 往 is only for direction, never for people.

examples.en: Go straight ahead and you'll get there.
We should learn from him.
This bus goes to Shanghai.
He smiled at me.

points.title: V着 — continuing state, existence
points.pattern: Place + Verb + 着 + Thing / Subject + Verb + 着
points.explain: 着 after a verb shows a state that continues, like 门开着 'the door is open'. In 'place + verb + 着 + thing' it describes what is there: 墙上挂着画. Pitfall: negate with 没, not 不.

examples.en: The door is open, come on in.
A map is hanging on the wall.
He's wearing a red shirt.
There are many books on the table.

points.title: V1着 V2 — doing while doing
points.explain: V1着 V2 means doing V2 while in the state of V1. V1 describes the manner, like 笑着说 'say with a smile'. Pitfall: the main action is V2, not V1.

examples.en: He said with a smile that it was fine.
Let's walk there.
Don't eat standing, sit down.
The child cried looking for mom.

points.title: 快要/就要…了 — about to
points.pattern: Subject + 快(要)/就要 + Verb + 了
points.explain: 快要…了 and 就要…了 mean something is about to happen. 就要 can follow a time word, but 快要 cannot. Pitfall: 明天快要走了 is wrong; say 明天就要走了.

examples.en: The train is about to leave.
We have an exam tomorrow.
It's almost dark, let's go home.
Spring Festival is coming soon.

points.title: 就 vs 才 — early vs late
points.pattern: Time + 就 + Verb + 了 / Time + 才 + Verb
points.short: early 就 vs late 才
points.explain: After a time or amount, 就 means it happened earlier or more easily than expected, and 才 means later or harder. 就 sentences often end in 了, but 才 sentences don't. Pitfall: don't add 了 after 才 + verb.

examples.en: He got up as early as six.
He didn't get up until ten.

examples.text: 我等了一个小时他才来。
examples.en: I waited an hour before he came.
I understood after reading it once.

points.title: Verb measure words: 次/遍/趟/下
points.pattern: Verb + Number + 次/遍/趟/下 (+ Object)
points.short: how many times: 次, 遍, 趟
points.explain: Verb measure words count how many times an action happens. 次 is general, 遍 means doing it from start to finish, 趟 is a round trip, and 下 is a brief action. Pitfall: a pronoun object goes before the measure word: 找过他两次.

examples.en: I've read this book three times.
I've been to Beijing twice.
I have to make a trip to the bank.
Please wait here a moment.

points.title: Duration complements
points.explain: The length of an action comes after the verb: 我学了两年中文. If there is an object, repeat the verb or put the time before the object. Pitfall: 我两年学中文 is wrong.

examples.en: I studied Chinese for two years.
He slept for eight hours.
I waited for you for ages.
I've been in China for a year.

points.title: Adjective reduplication AABB / AA
points.explain: Doubling an adjective (AA or AABB) makes it more vivid and is often followed by 的 or 地. Two-syllable adjectives double as AABB: 干干净净. Pitfall: doubled adjectives can't take 很 or 不.

examples.text: 房间打扫得干干净净的。
examples.en: The room was cleaned spotless.
She has big, big eyes.

examples.text: 大家高高兴兴地回家了。
examples.en: Everyone went home happily.
You should speak slowly.

points.title: Verb reduplication ABAB / V一V
points.explain: Doubling a verb makes the action short, casual or a gentle try: 看看, 看一看, 休息休息. For past actions, put 了 in the middle: 看了看. Pitfall: two-syllable verbs double as ABAB, not AABB.

examples.en: Try on this piece of clothing.
Let's take a little rest.
He glanced at his watch.
Let me think about it again.

points.title: Measure word reduplication — every
points.explain: Doubling a measure word or one-syllable noun means 'every': 人人 'everyone', 天天 'every day'. It is often followed by 都. Pitfall: it isn't used after numbers or 这/那.

examples.en: I exercise every day.
Everyone here knows him.
Every one of his clothes is expensive.
He practiced again and again.

points.title: Question words as 'any' + 都/也
points.explain: A question word with 都 or 也 means 'any' or 'every': 谁都 'everyone', 什么都不 'nothing'. Two question words can also match each other: 想吃什么就吃什么. Pitfall: the question word goes before 都/也 and the verb.

examples.en: I don't want to eat anything.
He's been everywhere.
Nobody knows about this.
Order whatever you want to eat.

points.title: 一点儿也/都不 — not at all
points.pattern: 一点儿 + 也/都 + 不/没 + Verb/Adj
points.short: not at all: 一点儿也不
points.explain: 一点儿也不 or 一点儿都不 means 'not at all'. It goes before the adjective or verb. Pitfall: 我不一点儿累 is wrong; say 我一点儿也不累.

examples.en: I'm not tired at all.
This dish isn't expensive at all.
He hasn't changed at all.
I'm not afraid at all.

points.title: 再也不/没 — never again
points.pattern: Subject + 再也 + 不/没 + Verb
points.explain: 再也不 means 'never again' from now on, and 再也没 means 'never again' since a past time. 再也 comes before the negative. Pitfall: 不再 just means 'no longer' and is softer.

examples.en: I'll never drink again.

examples.text: 他走了以后再也没回来。
examples.en: After he left, he never came back.
I'll never trust him again.

examples.text: 那以后我再也没见过她。
examples.en: I never saw her again after that.

points.title: 差点儿 — almost
points.explain: 差点儿 means 'almost' or 'nearly'. For bad things, 差点儿 and 差点儿没 both mean it didn't happen. For hoped-for things, 差点儿没 means it just barely happened. Pitfall: don't put 了 right after 差点儿; it goes after the verb.

examples.en: I was almost late.
He nearly burst into tears.

examples.text: 我差点儿忘了你的生日。
examples.en: I almost forgot your birthday.
I barely caught the train.

points.title: 终于 — finally
points.explain: 终于 means 'finally', after a long wait or effort, and usually describes a result someone wanted. The sentence often ends with 了. Pitfall: don't use 终于 for 'lastly' in a list; use 最后.

examples.en: I finally found a job.
The rain outside finally stopped.
He finally understood.
After waiting ages, the bus finally came.

points.title: 原来 — so it turns out
points.pattern: 原来 + Discovery / 原来的 + Noun
points.explain: 原来 can mean 'it turns out', when you discover a truth, or 'originally' or 'formerly'. As 'it turns out', it often starts the sentence. Pitfall: 本来 can also mean 'originally', but it doesn't mean 'it turns out'.

examples.en: Oh, so it's you who came!
So he's a teacher.
He still lives in the same place.
So you knew all along.

points.title: 本来 — originally, should have
points.explain: 本来 means 'originally' and is often followed by a change with 可是 or 后来. 本来就 means 'of course, it was always so'. Pitfall: 本来 suggests a plan that changed, so the second part shows the change.

examples.text: 我本来想去，可是太忙了。
examples.en: I meant to go, but I was too busy.
He originally didn't like dogs.
This was your fault in the first place.
I originally lived in Shanghai.

points.title: 其实 — actually
points.explain: 其实 means 'actually' or 'in fact' and shows the real situation, often different from what was thought. It can go before or after the subject. Pitfall: it is not used for 'currently' or 'at the moment'.

examples.en: Actually, I don't like meat.
This problem is actually simple.

examples.text: 他看起来很冷，其实人很好。
examples.en: He seems cold, but he's actually nice.
Actually, I knew long ago.

points.title: 只好 — have no choice but to
points.explain: 只好 means 'have no choice but to' and shows a decision made because there was no better option. The reason usually comes first. Pitfall: it goes before the verb, not before the subject.

examples.text: 没有车了，我只好走回家。
examples.en: No more buses, so I had to walk home.
It rained, so we had to stay home.

examples.text: 票卖完了，他只好明天来。
examples.en: Tickets sold out; he has to come tomorrow.
I couldn't do it, so I had to ask the teacher.

points.title: 不得不 — have to (forced)
points.explain: 不得不 means 'have to' or 'can't help but', when outside pressure forces you. It is stronger than 只好. Pitfall: it already includes a double negative, so don't add another 不.

examples.en: I have to get up early.

examples.text: 天太晚了，我不得不走了。
examples.en: It's too late; I must leave.
He's sick and has to be hospitalized.
We were forced to change our plan.

points.title: 千万 — be sure to, by all means
points.pattern: 千万 + 要/别/不要 + Verb
points.explain: 千万 means 'be sure to' or 'by all means' and adds strong urging, often in warnings with 别 or 不要. It is used in advice to others. Pitfall: don't use it to describe your own past actions.

examples.en: Whatever you do, don't forget.
Be very careful on the road!
Don't tell him, whatever you do.
Don't be late for the exam, whatever happens.

points.title: 到底 — after all; on earth
points.explain: 到底 in a question means 'on earth' or 'exactly' and pushes for a clear answer. In statements, it can mean 'finally' or 'after all'. Pitfall: in a question, don't add 吗; use a question word or A不A.

examples.en: Are you going or not?
What on earth is going on?
What exactly does he want?
Which one do you actually like?

points.title: 却 — but, yet
points.explain: 却 means 'but' or 'yet' and shows contrast. It is an adverb, so it goes after the subject and before the verb. Pitfall: unlike 但是, 却 can't go before the subject.

examples.en: He's smart but doesn't work hard.
I waited long, yet he didn't come.
It's cheap, yet it works well.
Everyone went, but he didn't.

points.title: 否则/不然 — otherwise
points.explain: 否则 and 不然 mean 'otherwise' and introduce what will happen if the first part isn't done. 否则 is more formal, and 不然 is more spoken. Pitfall: the first part is usually advice or a must.

examples.en: Let's hurry, or we'll be late.

examples.text: 你要多穿衣服，否则会感冒。
examples.en: Dress warmly, otherwise you'll catch a cold.
Eat up, or the food will get cold.

examples.text: 必须早点去，否则没票了。
examples.en: You must go early, or there'll be no tickets.

points.title: 万一 — in case, what if
points.explain: 万一 means 'in case' or 'what if' for an unlikely but possible bad event. It is often followed by 怎么办 or by advice. Pitfall: use 如果 for normal conditions and 万一 for unlikely bad ones.

examples.en: What if it rains?
Take an umbrella, just in case it rains.

examples.text: 万一他不来，我们就先走。
examples.en: If by chance he doesn't come, we'll leave first.

examples.text: 万一迷路了，就给我打电话。
examples.en: If you get lost, call me.

points.title: 有的…有的… — some … others
points.pattern: 有的 + Noun + A，有的 + B
points.explain: 有的…有的… means 'some … others …' and divides a group into parts. It always comes before the subject or noun. Pitfall: 有的 must go at the front of its clause, not after the verb.

examples.text: 有的人喜欢茶，有的人喜欢咖啡。
examples.en: Some like tea, some like coffee.

examples.text: 同学们有的唱歌，有的跳舞。
examples.en: Some classmates sang, others danced.
Some of these books are new, some old.

examples.text: 有的菜好吃，有的不好吃。
examples.en: Some dishes are tasty, others not.

points.title: 多/左右/上下 — approximately
points.pattern: Number + 多 + Measure / Number + 左右
points.short: about or more than: 多, 左右
points.explain: 多 after a number means 'more than' or 'odd': 十多个 'ten-odd'. 左右 after a number means 'about'. Pitfall: with round numbers like 10 or 20, 多 goes before the measure word; with other numbers, it goes after: 三个多月.

examples.en: I waited over twenty minutes.
He'll arrive around three.
I've been here for over a month.
This piece of clothing is about 100 yuan.

points.title: 几乎 — almost, nearly
points.pattern: Subject + 几乎 + 都/没 + Verb
points.explain: 几乎 means 'almost' or 'nearly' and is often followed by 都, 每 or a negative. It is more neutral than 差点儿. Pitfall: 几乎 describes a near-total amount, while 差点儿 is about an event that almost happened.

examples.en: I drink coffee almost every day.
Almost everyone is here.
I barely recognized him.
I hardly slept last night.
